fixture: Short full-modulator transistor-level transient (issue #125, DR-001 item 2): design/modulator/modulator.spice with design/ota/ota_fd.spice and design/modulator/comparator/comparator.spice, ideal DR-005 boundary sources, a coherent single tone at -6 dBFS and the 5.12 MHz clock.
result_kind: simulated (ngspice, transistor-level netlists of the assembled modulator; not the behavioural model, not measured silicon)

record_length.chosen_because: Cost. Measured on the dispatch host before any corner ran: about 3.1 s of ngspice per microsecond of transient at tt/27 C/1.80 V with a 1 ns maximum timestep, i.e. about 0.61 s per modulator clock. 1088 clocks is ~11 min at tt and ~22 min at a corner twice as slow, inside the batch fleet's 3600 s whole-job ceiling with margin. DR-001 item 2 requires the length to be stated; this is that statement, written into make_request.py before the first result.

sndr.why_not: No SNDR is claimed from this record. An in-band figure needs bins inside the 20 kHz band of spec row 1; 1024 modulator clocks give a bin bandwidth of 5000 Hz on the bitstream and only 8 output samples after decimation by the OSR, so neither route resolves the band. Spec sec 1.2's row 2 claim is a B-model result with the DR-001 cross-check; this bench supplies the cross-check's transistor-level side as bitstreams and integrator waveforms, not as an SNDR.

corner_set.name: DR-002 anchor set
corner_set.subset_statement: A declared subset of the DR-002 full 45-point grid: DR-002 names the anchor set for the expensive runs and lists the short full-modulator transient as one of them. This record is an anchor-subset result and is not a full-grid result.

limits.p_ana_definition: Time-weighted mean over the recorded clocks of the power delivered by the VDDA source plus the two reference sources. The 5 uA bias current is drawn from vdda, so it is inside the VDDA term. The vcm source is reported as p_vcm and is NOT in this sum.
limits.swing_source: spec/modulator-adc.md sec 5.4: the integrator outputs 'stay well inside the ~1.39 Vpp output swing sky130-opamp reports at its worst corner'. That sentence is the only swing figure the ratified spec gives and no new number is introduced here. It is applied to the DIFFERENTIAL integrator output, which is how design/ota/SIZING.md 'Swing vs spec 5.4' reads it (it compares ~2.3 Vpp differential of static headroom against it). The single-ended extremes are reported beside it, ungraded, so the other reading of the sentence stays visible. It is the CONTINUOUS-TIME extreme over the window, which is what the amplifier has to deliver; the per-clock samples in samples/ are the held states and have a smaller peak-to-peak, because they skip the switching transients between sample instants. The two are not in conflict and neither replaces the other.
limits.row_12_coverage: Row 12 (supply 1.62-1.98 V) is covered by the anchor set spanning 1.620, 1.800 and 1.980 V, not by a limit of its own.

boundary.note: DR-005: the reference, vcm and bias are ideal inputs at the boundary. vcm is held at 0.9 V on every corner and does not track Vdda, as in the other transistor-level benches here.

input_sequence.full_scale_note: Model B's full scale is the 1.2 V differential reference (sim/bmodel/model.py); -6 dBFS is 0.6 V peak differential, which is spec row 11's 0.5*VREF and the operating point spec sec 5.4 derives the swing from.
input_sequence.waveform: u(t) = 2*amplitude_peak_per_side_V * sin(2*pi*tone_hz*t), differential, t in seconds from the start of the transient; vinp = 0.9 + A*sin, vinn = 0.9 - A*sin
input_sequence.clock_source: Vclk PULSE, first rising 50 % crossing at 1.01e-08 s, period 1.953125e-07 s, 50 % duty, 0.2 ns edges, rescaled per corner to that corner's Vdda (corners.supply_waveforms)
input_sequence.input_sampling_edge: The input is sampled by the integrator cell during phi1, bottom plate first: phi1e falls before phi1 (design/modulator/README.md). phi1 is high while clk is low, so clock k samples the input around t = TRISE0 + (k + 0.5 .. 1.0)*Tclk; the exact instant is clkgen's phi1e falling edge and is corner dependent. u[n] in the samples files is the continuous-time differential input evaluated at the sample instant below, not at phi1e's fall: it is the analytic tone, so a sibling that wants another instant computes it from `waveform` directly.
input_sequence.sample_instant: Each committed per-clock value is a .meas FIND of the held node at t = TRISE0 + (k + 0.5)*Tclk, clock k's falling 50 % crossing of the clk source. That is the end of the phi2 integrate phase and a few hundred ps before clkgen lowers phi2, so both integrator outputs carry the charge that clock transferred and are still driven.
input_sequence.bitstream_polarity: bs high = the comparator decided y = +1 (bs and dp are both buffered from the latch node q; design/modulator/README.md). `y` in the samples files is +1 where bs_v > Vdda/2.
